To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) HRM systems have a positive impact on both intermediate outcomes (turnover, productivity) and corporate financial performance, 2) the impact of HRM on corporate financial performance is partially mediated by the impact of HR on intermediate outcomes, 3) the impact of the HRM system is in part contingent upon the degree to which it is aligned with competitive strategy, and 4) HRM systems can be differentiated by the presence and strength of various components.

high performance work systems (HPWS) are associated with improved financial performance, and that the effect of HPWS on financial performance is stronger in firms that are more focused on product differentiation.
high performance work practices have a positive and significant effect on both intermediate employee and long-term financial outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of HRM practices on employee and corporate performance. We have focused on the following questions
the effects of human resource management practices on employee attitudes and behaviors, and on firm performance.
the impact of human resource (HR) management practices on the performance of organizations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence supports the contention that high performance work practices (HPWPs), which include a range of HRM policies, practices, and systems, have a positive impact on firm performance.
HRM has no impact on firm performance.
the evidence supports a positive relationship between the use of High Performance Work Systems (HPWS) and the performance of the organization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HRM policies and practices are important to the performance of organizations.
high performance work practices have a positive impact on firm performance, but that the impact of individual practices varies across firms.
there is a positive relationship between high performance work systems (HPWS) and firm performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are a number of HRM practices that are associated with improved performance, but the impact is small.

the impact of HRM on firm performance is contingent on the nature and quality of HR practices, the extent to which they are implemented, and the extent to which the firm has a competitive strategy that supports the use of HR practices.
HRM practices have a significant impact on the performance of firms, and this is true even after controlling for other factors that affect firm performance.
